dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

prototype_evidence.known_prior_scope: Known equiatomic NbTaZr alloy phase separation and2023 theoretical source are acknowledged; no exact three-site ordered SC experimental benchmark identified in bounded primary search. Not a first material discovery.

candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: All ten lambda gains41.39-46.95%, separate source Eli Tc17.517 versus13.697K (+27.89%). Target coarse force~0.00010eV/A supports the published coarse-relaxed double-grid model; fine force0.04583eV/A is substantial sensitivity. Target fine E is16.23meV/site higher; known equiatomic alloy shows Nb/Ta-rich and Zr-rich BCC plus Zr-rich HCP competition. Conditional Gamma harmonic displacement estimate is not fine relaxation or EPC error certification. Evaluated risks define a falsifiable bounded hypothesis, not an established bulk ground state or experimental coherence proof.
candidate.ambient_scope: Source nearambient fullstress/pressure and coarse-relaxed geometry, positive raw-Gamma optical compression beyond printing bounds, and no negative printed finite-path values support preliminary local feasibility only within the declared source approximation. WholeBZ/global hull/synthesis remain unknown.
candidate.route_response: Cross-species R4 coordination6 versus5 and Zr periodic distance2.96840 versus3.34686A; source SCF is the EPC anchor. CIF/geo basal reflection has det-1 and is retained as scalar parity equivalence, not a proper-rotation proof. Computed source EPC response is associated with construction; pure geometry-only causality and converged numerical uplift are unproved.
candidate.next_action: Test fine-geometry retention/EPC ordering on the two exact states; assess specific Nb/Ta-rich and Zr-rich BCC/HCP competitors or a concrete constrained/metastable preparation route.
